name: Space Age couture
summary: The Paris couture of 1964 to 1970 that took its look from the space race. It uses white and silver, short A-line dresses and flat trousers. It also has vinyl, plastic and metal discs, and low boots with a visor or helmet hat.

philosophy.core_thesis: Dress for the future shows clean, geometric lines and new materials. The body moves free in a short, flat, hard-edged shape of white, silver and plastic.
design_principles: Cut the hem 10 to 15 cm above the knee on a day dress, and keep the skirt in a plain A-line.
Make each seam a visible line, with a flat welt or a top-stitched seam in a contrast colour.
Choose a stiff cloth with body, such as heavy gabardine, that holds the A-line away from the leg.
Use white, silver and one bright colour, and keep the plain areas wide.
Cut a window, a circle or a square into the dress, so that the shape is geometric.
Join plastic or metal discs of 5 to 8 cm with small rings in place of thread.
Finish with flat boots, a visor or a helmet cap, and tinted glasses.
anti_patterns: A fitted waist with a full petticoat skirt
A high heel and a long skirt
Visible hand sewing and a worn, aged cloth

silhouette.shape: A short A-line or a straight tunic with a flat bust and no waist, worn with straight trousers and flat boots.
silhouette.line: A straight shoulder, a high empire or no waist, and a hem 10 to 15 cm above the knee.
silhouette.fit: Free of the body at the waist and hip; the stiff cloth stands away and does not cling.
silhouette.proportion: Hem 10 to 15 cm above the knee. Trouser leg straight and ankle-length. Boot heel 2 to 3 cm. Hat brim or visor 4 to 6 cm.
rules: Cut the dress in a trapeze that opens from the shoulder to the hem.
Set a seam or a welt in a different colour so that it draws the shape.
Pair a short dress with flat white boots and tinted glasses.
Keep a plain neck and no collar, or a small round collar.
Make a metal-disc dress as a short, sleeveless shift.

fabrics.rule: Choose a cloth or a material of the new age. Use stiff wool gabardine for the day, then vinyl, plastic discs and metal rings for the show.

methods: heavy gabardine cut flat with welted seams
top-stitched seams in a contrast colour
plastic or metal discs joined with ring links
construction.closures: A concealed zip or a flat front button band; vinyl coats close with a plain press stud.
construction.details: A helmet cap or a visor, tinted glasses, flat white boots, and a small cut-out circle on the waist or the back.

surface.pattern: Plain white or one bright colour; a geometric block of two colours; for the show, a sheet of linked discs.
surface.gloss: Gabardine at 2–5 GU; vinyl and lacquer at 60–90 GU; polished aluminium at 80–100 GU.
surface.wear: The style wants a clean, new surface; a creased, soiled or faded piece loses the effect.

palette.strategy: White and silver as the base, with one bright accent colour and black for the line.

processes: haute couture to the measure of the client
flat pattern cutting in the atelier
linking of discs by hand with pliers
making.scale: Haute couture in the house, then a ready-to-wear line; licensed copies sold in department stores from 1965.
making.signs: Flat welted seams, ring links between the discs, and a clean edge with no visible hand stitch.

pieces.form: Short A-line dress with welted contrast seams
Straight ankle-length trousers with a flat front
Sleeveless shift of linked metal discs
Short boxy coat of white vinyl with a flat collar
Knit tunic with a bold geometric block

evidence.title: André Courrèges dress and coat, c.1966
evidence.credit: Photographer for the Rhode Island School of Design Museum of Art

evidence.title: 1969 Pierre Cardin little black cocktail dress with chrome metal detail 01
evidence.credit: Photographer for the Rhode Island School of Design Museum of Art

emotion.target_response: A sense of speed and a clean future: the viewer sees a hard, bright shape that has no past.

use_cases: a period costume brief for a 1960s film
a retro-future costume for a science fiction stage show
a study note on 1960s Paris couture
avoid_when: the brief wants a soft, romantic or historic dress
the brief needs a long, fitted evening dress
the brief is a modern technical shell or sportswear

modifiers.how: Drop the metal and vinyl, keep the short A-line, and use wool crepe with bold print.
Remove the contrast seams and the discs, keep a flat shape in one plain cloth.
Swap the stiff cloth for soft cotton, lengthen the hem, and add embroidery.

ornament_level.note: Day pieces are plain; a disc dress is the ornament.
